subject: Re: Service provider role confirmation & encryption evidence request (CCPA/CPRA addendum)
messages:
From: Lidia Cortez <lidia.cortez@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Service provider role confirmation & encryption evidence request (CCPA/CPRA addendum)

Team — thanks for sending the initial addendum. A few high-priority asks from AcmeHealth legal and privacy before we can take this to procurement: 

1) Please confirm in writing that Redwood will be classified as a "Service Provider" under CCPA/CPRA (not an "Operator"), and that you will not engage in "selling" as defined by statute. Our legal needs explicit language we can reference in the addendum.

2) We need evidence of encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and a short statement of key management for customer data. A PDF or link to a short artifact is fine (we don't need full SOC pages).

3) Subprocessor notices: Acme requires a minimum of 30 calendar days' notice for new subprocessors that will process Acme data, plus emergency onboarding exceptions with documented approvals. Can you confirm notice windows and the emergency onboarding process?

4) Onshore fallback: because we process regulated PHI-adjacent data, Acme prefers an onshore fallback plan (US-only processing) if offshore subprocessors are unavailable. Please outline options and timing.

I've attached a redline from our counsel with suggested markups (Acme_CCPR_addendum_changes_v1.docx). Would you be able to confirm next steps this week?

Best,
Lidia Cortez
Head of Privacy & Compliance
AcmeHealth

Attachments: Acme_CCPR_addendum_changes_v1.docx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lidia Cortez <lidia.cortez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service provider role confirmation & encryption evidence request (CCPA/CPRA addendum)

Lidia — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline: 

1) Service provider status: yes — Redwood will accept Service Provider designation for the purposes of the CCPA/CPRA addendum. We'll draft explicit binding language mirroring your counsel's phrasing and propose it in the next redline.

2) Encryption evidence: Ben (cc'd) can provide the short evidence artifact (certificate-style PDF) showing TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and a KMS outline. We'll attach a one-page proof rather than the full SOC documents.

3) Subprocessor notice: standard is 30 days for non-emergency; emergency onboarding we can do with documented approvals and a post-hoc notice within 5 business days. We can accept 30-day notice as a firm term.

4) Onshore fallback: we have two fallback modes — (A) soft-fallback: route Acme workload to US-only regions automatically when offshore capacity is constrained (short delay), or (B) dedicated onshore pool as a reserved capacity option (requires a modest commit). I'll ask Ben to outline typical failover timing and steps.

We'll prepare an internal redline to your draft and return a tracked-change document by EOD Thursday (Feb 19). If that timing doesn't work, tell me a firm cutoff.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Hi Lidia / Jordan — technical follow-up and artifacts attached. Summary below and point-by-point mapping to Acme's asks: 

- Service provider role: Product & Legal confirm runtime is only used to provide inference for customer prompts; no network of re-selling or combining with third-party datasets. We will include a declarative clause in the addendum.

- Encryption in transit and at rest: we use TLS1.3 for all client-server connections; tokens are transmitted over TLS and persisted encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Our KMS is customer-key-capable (we support BYOK via KMS integration) — see attached redwood-encryption-proofs-2026.pdf. That document includes: 
  * TLS cert chain sample (not private keys)
  * At-rest encryption description + key rotation cadence
  * KMS integration summary and how customers can verify key control

- Subprocessor notices: our standard contract provides 30-calendar-day notice for non-emergency subprocessor additions. For emergency onboarding (critical security patching, capacity outages), our on-call approval flow captures decision and we push a notice within 72 hours; we can accept Acme's request for a 5-business-day post-hoc report instead. We will include an escalation workflow in the addendum appendix.

- Onshore fallback: two implementation options (as Jordan noted). Typical soft-fallback window is 2–6 hours for failover in standard hosted mode; dedicated onshore pool is immediate once provisioned (provisioning lead time depends on reserved capacity status). If Acme needs guaranteed immediate US-only processing, we recommend Dedicated capacity.

I've uploaded the artifact to our secure drive for your legal team: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/ccpa-evidence/acme-enc-proofs (PDF also attached). Let me know if you need anything more formal (signed attestation).

Regards,
Ben Carter
Principal Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-encryption-proofs-2026.pdf

Thanks Jordan and Ben — that helps a lot. Acme legal reviewed the PDF and the notes; two follow-ups required before procurement signs: 

• Please add explicit language in the addendum that Redwood will notify and provide an attestation for any change to the KMS configuration that would materially affect customer key control.

• For the emergency subprocessor exception, Acme requires a documented approval path and a single point of contact for escalation. Can you provide the SRE on-call alias and an escalation contact?

Assuming you can accept the attestation language and provide the escalation contact, procurement will prepare DocuSign for the revised addendum. We're targeting execution by next Friday (Mar 5). Can you confirm you can meet that timeline?

If yes, please send the revised tracked document and a DocuSign-ready PDF to privacy@acmehealth.com and myself.

Best,
Lidia Cortez
Head of Privacy & Compliance
AcmeHealth
